issues.legal_issue: Laws inserted into the Ninth Schedule through constitutional amendments made after the basic-structure limitation arose are subject to judicial review for their effect on fundamental rights and the basic structure.
material_facts: The challenged matters concerned laws inserted into the Ninth Schedule by constitutional amendments made after the basic-structure doctrine had been propounded.
Some laws had previously been found unconstitutional, in whole or in part, while others were not connected with agrarian reform.
The challenge concerned whether Article 31B could give those laws complete immunity from review under Part III.
issues.conclusion: A post-threshold Ninth Schedule insertion does not confer blanket immunity. The law must be tested for infringement of Part III rights and whether the infringement damages or destroys the basic structure; if it does, the law is invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Articles 31B and 368 must be read subject to the implied limitation imposed by the basic-structure doctrine. A court applies the direct impact and effect, or rights, test: it first determines whether the law infringes Part III, then whether that infringement damages or destroys the basic structure. The assessment includes the nature and extent of the infringement and the essence of the right, viewed across Part III. The Court relied on Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain, Waman Rao v. Union of India, Minerva Mills v. Union of India, and L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India, among other authorities.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_schedule_insertion and post_threshold_schedule_insertion and law_infringes_part_three and infringement_damages_basic_structure

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_schedule_ins: A party challenges the constitutional validity of a law's inclusion in the protected constitutional schedule.
predicates.post_threshold_schedule_insertion: A constitutional amendment places the law in the schedule after the basic-structure limitation on amendment applies.
predicates.law_infringes_part_three: The law takes away or abridges a right protected by the fundamental-rights chapter.
predicates.infringement_damages_basic_structure: The infringement, assessed by its actual impact and effect, damages or destroys an essential feature of the Constitution.

issues.definition: When a challenged schedule insertion made after the amendment power became limited results in a rights infringement that damages the basic structure, the protected law is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A Ninth Schedule law whose validity has already been upheld by the Supreme Court cannot ordinarily be challenged again under the principles stated in this judgment, subject to the stated exception for a later insertion of a law previously held to violate Part III.
material_facts: The Court addressed the effect of a prior Supreme Court decision upholding the validity of a Ninth Schedule law.
It separately considered a law that had been held to violate a Part III right and was subsequently placed in the Ninth Schedule after the basic-structure limitation arose.
issues.conclusion: A law whose validity has already been upheld by the Supreme Court cannot be challenged again on the principles stated in this judgment. A previously identified Part III violation remains open to challenge if the law is later inserted into the Ninth Schedule after the basic-structure limitation arose.
issues.legal_principle: The Court's rule on the finality of a prior Supreme Court upholding does not foreclose the expressly stated exception for a law held to violate Part III and subsequently inserted into the Ninth Schedule after the basic-structure limitation arose. That exception follows the review principles in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain, and Waman Rao v. Union of India.

predicates.ninth_schedule_law_challenge: A party brings a constitutional challenge to a law placed in the protected constitutional schedule.
predicates.prior_supreme_court_upholding: The Supreme Court has already upheld the validity of that law.
predicates.later_insertion_of_previously_violative_: After the basic-structure limitation arose, the law was placed in the schedule despite having previously been held to violate a Part III right.

issues.definition: A challenge to a schedule law already upheld by the Supreme Court is precluded unless the law falls within the stated exception for a later insertion after a prior finding of a Part III violation.

issues.legal_issue: Actions taken and transactions finalized under the challenged laws are not open to challenge as a result of the principles stated in this judgment.
material_facts: The Court considered the consequences of applying its ruling to actions already taken and transactions already finalized under the challenged laws.
issues.conclusion: Actions taken and transactions finalized as a result of the challenged laws are not open to challenge.
issues.legal_principle: In stating the consequences of its ruling on the constitutional reference, the Court expressly preserved actions taken and transactions finalized under the impugned laws from challenge.

predicates.ninth_schedule_law_challenge: A party challenges a law placed in the protected constitutional schedule.
predicates.action_or_transaction_finalized_under_ch: An action was taken or a transaction was completed as a result of the challenged law.

issues.definition: In a challenge to a schedule law, an action taken or transaction completed under that law is not open to challenge under the Court's ruling.
